pages.text: The liquid fuel line in one sentence: $(4)liquefy → process → mix → can → burn$(0).$(br2)$(li)$(l:akaishi:fuel_liquefier)Energy Liquefier$(/l): squeezes solid ingredients into liquid energy$(li)$(l:akaishi:fuel_processor)Energy Processor$(/l): turns liquid energy into burnable fuel$(li)$(l:akaishi:fuel_mixer)Fuel Mixer$(/l): blends low-tier fuel into high-tier fuel$(li)$(l:akaishi:fuel_canner)Fuel Canner$(/l): pours liquid into fuel cells$(br2)Hand the filled cells to "$(l:akaishi:reactor)The Reactor$(/l)"; the very top fuel keeps climbing into "$(l:akaishi:plasma)Plasma Chain$(/l)". Recipes and stats for each machine live in their own entries — click through above.

$(bold)Line logistics:$(0)$(li)Fluid Tanks: Basic 16,000 mb / Advanced 64,000 mb / Super 256,000 mb — let output settle in a tank before feeding the next stage so machines never wait$(li)Fluid Pipe: moves $(4)4,000 mb/tick$(0) of any liquid — no discrimination$(br2)$(bold)Exception:$(0) exhausted fuel is corrosive and must ride the dedicated $(bold)Sealed Exhausted Pipe$(0); normal pipes refuse that cargo.$(br2)Its recycling route lives in "Secrets of Life" — until then, remember: $(4)don't dump it$(0).
Upstream sits "$(l:akaishi:fuel_system)Fuel & Cooling$(/l)", downstream "$(l:akaishi:reactor)The Reactor$(/l)"; this line's top product keeps condensing onward into the Plasma Chain.
